- Page: GitHub pull request
- URL: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/27058

- Commits: 20

...

## Features
`--enable-session-radix-cache` makes a **session a tag over ordinary evictable radix KV** — no `Session` object, no pinned slot, no timeout.
* A request carrying a `session_id` has its KV **tagged** in the radix cache — purely a release-grouping tag; the KV stays **LRU-neutral** and competes as ordinary radix.
* A single **`close`** RPC bulk-evicts everything tagged with that session — found by a scan at close.
There is **no `open`** step; the tag is the only session state.
* KV stays **ordinary evictable radix cache** : the pool can't be wedged, and a session under pressure is simply evicted and re-prefilled on its next turn.
* Opt-in alternative to `--enable-streaming-session` (which pins session KV in non-evictable slots) — avoids that path's worker-wedge under concurrent load and turn-over-turn context duplication, by construction.
```
--enable-session-radix-cache
```
Off by default; unset = no behavior change. Works under any `--radix-eviction-policy` (session KV is LRU-neutral). The feature lives in `radix_cache.py` (tag / release) and `scheduler.py` (the `req.session_id` tag + close routing); `SessionController` / `streaming_session.py` are bypassed when the flag is on.

## Design
Two touch points, both on the normal `RadixCache` — there is **no open / registration** step:
1. **Tag (data path).** A generate request carries `session_params.id` ; the scheduler stamps it onto a plain `Req` as `req.session_id` (no history reconstruction, no slot — reuse across turns is just radix prefix matching).
On KV insert the leaf is tagged ( `TreeNode.session_id` ) for release grouping; the node keeps its ordinary `req.priority` — a session is **not** a separate eviction class. The tag is the only per-session state.
2.
**Close (evict).** `close_session → release_session(id)` scans `evictable_leaves` for leaves tagged with the session and frees each one's **unique leaf→branch chain** in place; shared prefixes are branch points and are preserved.
A node tagged by multiple sessions carries the full holder set and is freed only when its **last** holder closes. The free is synchronous (no deferred queue) and touches only the session's own tagged chains. With no per-session index, a request that finishes after close has nothing to leak.
Session KV is ordinary evictable radix, so the pool can never be wedged — a still-open session under pressure is simply LRU-evicted and re-prefilled on its next turn.
```
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant Caller as Caller (Dynamo router / client)
    participant Sched as Scheduler
    participant Radix as RadixCache
    loop each turn (full context sent)
        Caller->>Sched: generate(session_id=sid)
        Sched->>Radix: insert KV
        Radix-->>Radix: tag leaf.session_id=sid (LRU-neutral)
    end
    Caller->>Sched: close_session(sid)
    Sched->>Radix: release_session(sid)
    Radix-->>Radix: scan evictable_leaves for sid, free each tagged chain
    Note over Radix: free each session's unique leaf→branch chain, shared prefixes (branch points) preserved
```
Loading
Because the KV is always ordinary evictable radix KV, nothing is pinned — the pool can't be wedged by session KV. The session tag is **eviction-policy-neutral by default** ; a per-session demote / protect hint (RFC [#27574](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/27574) ) can override that later.

## Performance
Measured on the actual subagent workload: **N concurrent pi orchestrators, each delegating to 4 worker subagents** (one session per subagent, opened on first turn, closed on `agent_end` ). Same client workload in both arms — only `--enable-session-radix-cache` differs.

...

| metric | plain radix (OFF) | session radix cache (ON) |
| peak pool occupancy | **100% — 0 free tokens** | 64% |
| peak resident cached KV | 100% | 53% |
| forced LRU evictions (cache thrash) | **284,544 tokens** | **0** |
| session-close releases | 0 | 82 |
Without the feature, 12 concurrent agents **saturate** the KV pool (0 free tokens) and the radix cache thrashes — 285K tokens force-evicted by LRU, cached prefixes that then have to be re-prefilled.
With it, each subagent's `close` frees that session's KV first, so the pool peaks at 64%, holds ~36% free throughout, and triggers **zero** pressure evictions.
A lighter 8-agent homogeneous run shows the same shape — OFF climbs to 94% and pins at 85% resident, ON drains to 24% as sessions close ( [chart](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ishandhanani/73efce1007118ea08ebea0c2f83879a3/raw/kv-pressure-homogeneous-N8.png) ).

...

* _Transparency_ : greedy (temp 0) answer byte-identical with vs without a session — tagging never touches logits.
* _Shared-prefix_ : sessions A/B share a 6.6K-token prefix; close(A) frees only A's unique chain (A's re-sent prompt drops to `cached=|shared|` ), while B's KV and the shared prefix stay resident (cache-hit probes).
* _Reclamation (engine truth)_ : each close logs `release_session <id>: freed N nodes` (the tagged leaves found by scanning `evictable_leaves` ); re-sending a closed 15K-token session is a **cache miss** ( `cached_tokens → 0` ).
* _Robustness 4/4_ : close-unopened, double-close, re-open same id, close-while-in-flight — all graceful, worker alive.
* _Oversubscription_ : 12 × 21K-token sessions (~252K > 144K pool) opened without closing — all served, ping flat 63–68 ms, no wedge.

...

## How to reproduce
Launch the server with the flags (sglang directly, or via the Dynamo backend in [ai-dynamo/dynamo](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/10214) ):
```
python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path <model> \
  --enable-session-radix-cache --radix-eviction-policy priority --enable-metrics
```
Drive **N concurrent sessions** , each: `open_session(sid)` → several `generate(session_id=sid)` with full context per turn → `close_session(sid)` . (Here: pi subagents over the Dynamo backend — one session per subagent, `close` on `agent_end` .)
A/B by toggling `--enable-session-radix-cache` , and watch `/metrics` :
* `sglang:kv_evictable_tokens` — resident cached KV (the residency oracle; **not** `kv_used_tokens` , which is running-request occupancy and drops to ~0 whenever generation finishes).
* `sglang:evicted_tokens_total{cache_type="RadixCache"}` — forced LRU evictions.
With the flag **on** this stays ~0 (session close frees first); **off** , it climbs as the pool saturates.
* the per-close log line `release_session <id>: freed N nodes` confirms the tag→close→release path end to end.

## Notes / open questions
* **Tag carrier:** the session id rides `session_params.id` today; a dedicated `session_id` field on `GenerateReqInput` would drop the reuse of the streaming-flavored `SessionParams` struct (touches `io_struct` + the router). Follow-up.
* **Priority:** session KV is **LRU-neutral** — a session is a release-grouping tag, not an eviction class.
A per-session demote (ephemeral subagent scratch / paused main-agent) or protect hint is a future surface (RFC [[Agentic Inference] Programmatic KV Cache for Agentic Workloads #27574](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/27574) ).
* **Shared-prefix accounting:** each node carries the **set** of sessions holding it, and close frees a node only once its last holder closes (branch points + sibling KV preserved).
A node physically shared by several sessions (byte-identical content → same leaf) is therefore freed on the last close, order-independent (review thread r3386637292).
* **Lineage:** pairs with the Dynamo backend wiring in [feat(sglang): derive radix sessions from trajectory ids ai-dynamo/dynamo](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/10214) , and is the first **session-membership + release** primitive of the agentic-KV RFC [[Agentic Inference] Programmatic KV Cache for Agentic
Workloads #27574](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/27574) (the addressing key its Share / Prefetch hints build on). Draft / RFC for shape feedback.

# [StreamingSession] Deadlock issues: unbounded / over-subscribed non-evictable session KV, no safe mid-session release
## Summary
`--enable-streaming-session` pins a session's KV in slots that are **lock-ref'd and invisible to radix eviction**. There is currently **no admission control and no per-session cap**: `SessionController.open()` never refuses, and a session's slot grows unbounded across turns.
Under realistic multi-session / multi-turn load this **deadlocks the worker**, and there is **no safe way to relieve the pressure by releasing a live session** — the obvious release path crashes the scheduler.

...

## Background: why pinned session KV can deadlock
Session KV is held with `lock_ref > 0`, so `unified_radix_cache` skips it during eviction. That is the point of streaming sessions (KV must survive between turns), but it means pinned session KV is **non-evictable**.
If the pinned set is allowed to grow past what the pool can hold, the scheduler cannot free pages to make forward progress — a classic hold-and-wait deadlock with no preemption.

...

## Two distinct causes
### Problem 2 — single-session runaway growth
```mermaid
    D --> F[radix cannot evict pinned KV]
    E --> F
    F --> G[scheduler cannot free pages -> deadlock]
```

## The hard limitation: no safe mid-session release
The intuitive fix — "under pressure, release/demote a live session's slot" — is **not safe today**. After turn 2+, a slot's lock sits on the session's own `_VirtualNode` (`StreamingSession.try_match_prefix` returns `last_device_node = slot.virtual_node`).
`release_session` then does `inner.dec_lock_ref(slot.last_node)` and throws:

...

Both a custom "demote ISOLATED->SHARED" and the intuitive "move it to radix and close it" hit this. `release_session` is only safe at **clean teardown** (the explicit close, or the reaper for timed-out sessions between batches).
There is **no safe mid-conversation "shrink / migrate this session" primitive** — which is the crux: any fix that must free a live session's pin mid-stream is blocked at the engine level.

## Possible fixes

# [StreamingSession] Deadlock issues: unbounded / over-subscribed non-evictable session KV, no safe mid-session release

- Page: GitHub issue
- URL: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/27024
- State: closed (completed)
- Author: ishandhanani
- Created: 2026-06-02T06:32:59Z
- Updated: 2026-06-02T09:23:00Z
- Repository: sgl-project/sglang
- Number: #27024
- Comments: 1

---

## Summary

`--enable-streaming-session` pins a session's KV in slots that are **lock-ref'd and invisible to radix eviction**. There is currently **no admission control and no per-session cap**: `SessionController.open()` never refuses, and a session's slot grows unbounded across turns. Under realistic multi-session / multi-turn load this **deadlocks the worker**, and there is **no safe way to relieve the pressure by releasing a live session** — the obvious release path crashes the scheduler.

We hit this driving streaming sessions from an agent runtime (one session per sub-agent, opened on the first turn, closed at sub-agent end) on GLM-4.7-Flash, TP2, 2x L40S. With a handful of concurrent sub-agents each holding ~15–30K tokens, `kv_available` goes to ~0 at 99% occupancy and the worker stops making progress.

## Background: why pinned session KV can deadlock

Session KV is held with `lock_ref > 0`, so `unified_radix_cache` skips it during eviction. That is the point of streaming sessions (KV must survive between turns), but it means pinned session KV is **non-evictable**. If the pinned set is allowed to grow past what the pool can hold, the scheduler cannot free pages to make forward progress — a classic hold-and-wait deadlock with no preemption.

## Two distinct causes

These need to be separated because **admission fixes the first but not the second**.

### Problem 1 — concurrent burst

N sessions pin simultaneously and `sum(held) > pool`. Each is individually reasonable; collectively they oversubscribe the non-evictable tier. The scheduler can't evict (all pinned) and stalls.

### Problem 2 — single-session runaway growth

One session grows unbounded across turns until its own pinned slot fills the pool. Admission does **not** help here: the session is admitted small and grows afterward. Observed directly — a sequential workload with only one active session still deadlocked at 99% occupancy because that single session's slot grew to ~120K.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[open streaming session] --> B[pin KV in slot, lock_ref>0]
    B --> C{pinned tier vs pool}
    C -->|N sessions, sum > pool| D[Problem 1: burst oversubscription]
    C -->|one session grows past pool| E[Problem 2: runaway growth]
    D --> F[radix cannot evict pinned KV]
    E --> F
    F --> G[scheduler cannot free pages -> deadlock]
```

## The hard limitation: no safe mid-session release

The intuitive fix — "under pressure, release/demote a live session's slot" — is **not safe today**. After turn 2+, a slot's lock sits on the session's own `_VirtualNode` (`StreamingSession.try_match_prefix` returns `last_device_node = slot.virtual_node`). `release_session` then does `inner.dec_lock_ref(slot.last_node)` and throws:

```
AttributeError: '_VirtualNode' object has no attribute 'lock_ref'
-> Scheduler hit an exception -> SIGQUIT -> worker dies -> subsequent requests 404
```

Both a custom "demote ISOLATED->SHARED" and the intuitive "move it to radix and close it" hit this. `release_session` is only safe at **clean teardown** (the explicit close, or the reaper for timed-out sessions between batches). There is **no safe mid-conversation "shrink / migrate this session" primitive** — which is the crux: any fix that must free a live session's pin mid-stream is blocked at the engine level.

## Possible fixes

The clean architectural split we landed on: **admission belongs in the session layer; eviction belongs in the radix cache.** Don't reimplement radix eviction inside the session manager.

1. **Admission at `open()` (fixes Problem 1).** Keep the pinned tier within a budget (a fraction of the KV pool). If reserving a new session would exceed budget, open it as an ordinary **evictable radix entry** instead of pinning it. The session still exists and is served normally; its KV just rides the radix tree, so a burst can no longer oversubscribe the non-evictable tier. With budget < pool there is always evictable headroom, so no burst deadlock by construction.

2. **Bounded per-session pin window (fixes Problem 2, correct form).** Never let a session pin more than a bounded window. At a clean turn boundary (`save_from_req`), keep the last `cap` tokens pinned and insert the cold prefix `[0, len-cap)` into the radix as evictable nodes. The slot never grows past `cap`, so there is never a runaway slot to release — it stays within the safe-boundary constraint above. This is the proper, crash-free fix for runaway growth; it is allocator/slot-level work.

   - A lighter-weight interim variant: at turn save, if the pinned tier just grew past budget, **flip the session to evictable (SHARED)** so its future turns ride the radix. This bounds future growth without trimming the already-pinned slot (freed at clean close), and avoids the unsafe mid-stream release.

3. **Let pinned KV participate in priority eviction / HiCache host demotion** so a pinned session can be *safely* demoted under pressure — this is the longer-term path that would also retire the "no safe mid-session release" limitation.

## Proposed first step

A PR implementing **(1) admission** plus the interim flavor of **(2) growth cap**, gated behind a budget env (`SGLANG_SESSION_KV_FRACTION`, default preserves legacy unbounded behavior when unset), with a CPU unit test covering both deadlock causes. Linked below. The full bounded-pin-window (2, correct form) and priority/HiCache participation (3) are follow-ups.

## Repro

Dynamo frontend `--router-mode kv` + NATS + sglang worker `--enable-streaming-session`, then either:
- **Problem 1:** > ~4 concurrent sessions each holding ~15–30K tokens (e.g. parallel agents), or
- **Problem 2:** one session that keeps growing across turns.

Occupancy climbs to ~99%, `kv_available` -> ~0, and the worker stops progressing. Attempting a live-session release to recover hits the `_VirtualNode` crash above.

## Environment

- sglang 0.5.12.post1, GLM-4.7-Flash, TP2, 2x L40S
- `--enable-streaming-session`, page-size 16

- Page: GitHub issue

- Number: #29099

- Assignees: stmatengss, ishandhanani

---

## 1. Motivation

SGLang's streaming session feature (`StreamingSession`) persists KV cache between turns. When a turn finishes, `cache_finished_req` saves the request's `req_pool_idx` and token indices into a `SessionSlot` dict instead of releasing them. The next turn restores this state instantly via `match_prefix`, bypassing the radix tree entirely.

The side effect is that idle session slots which are sessions waiting between turns hold pool resources **permanently and invisibly** until the client explicitly closes the session or an opt-in timeout fires. Under memory pressure a server with many idle sessions can OOM every new request while session KV stays pinned.

## 2. Limitations of the Current System

The problem of unbounded cache growth and deadlocks in current `StreamingSession` are well documented in this https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/27024

## 3. Design

We introduce **session-level KV preemption**: when the token pool runs low and tree eviction alone cannot satisfy demand, idle session slots are soft-evicted until enough tokens are freed. The session is not closed and only its KV is released. On the next turn the request re-prefills from whatever the radix tree still has cached; no error is surfaced to the client.

The design supports pluggable eviction heuristics (e.g. LRU, length-based, weighted length × recency). The initial implementation will provide **LRU** as the first heuristic: `preempt_session_kv` sorts idle candidates by `last_active_time` (a `time.monotonic()` timestamp recorded at turn-finish in `save_from_req`) and evicts oldest-first until the deficit is covered.

The benefit of  **heuristic extensibility** is that instead of being tightly coupled with the eviction policy of Radix Tree, which is agentic agnostics,  our `preempt_session_kv` interface enabling session-level agent-aware policies the tree cannot express:

- **Recency**: prefer evicting sessions that are cold and are unlikely to receive request soon.
- **Router-initialized signals**: For example, the router injects a priority score at session-open, so VIP or latency-SLA sessions will not be targets of eviction. This is closedly related to https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/27574.
- **Weighted combinations**: tunable combination of recency, size, and router signals.

### Fixing the problems of `StreamingSession`

One cause of the current [problem](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/27024) of `StreamingSession` seems to be the lack of **single source of truth**. Currently, cache-related states of each session are scatter into multiple classes: 
- `SessionSlot`: holds `req_pool_idx`, `kv_allocated_len`, `cache_protected_len`, and `last_node`
- `ReqToTokenPool`: maps `req_pool_idx` to physical KV page indices
- `RadixTree`: holds the same page indices for the shared prefix under a `lock_ref`
Each class is mutating and reading these state and it is hard to keep the updates in sync. 

One way to solve this problem is to have **session-private Prefix Cache**: instead of having all sessions share a single Prefix Cache, initialize one PrefixCache per session whose only role is prefix matching. All other cache-related logic are handled by the `SessionSlot`, which uses `TokenToKVPoolAllocator` to allocate and free pages, and the lifecycle of kv cache is tied to the `SessionSlot` object itself so that we can support session level eviction safely. The tradeoff here is we no longer have inter-session prefix matching, yet this is acceptable because in agentic workloads, most matches happen inside session accorss turns.

However, implementing session-private cache might involve non-trivial refactors of the `Schduler` and `SchdulerBatch`. I am currently trying to come up with a less intrusive approach. We are open to implementing this RFC on top of whichever session architecture the maintainers prefer, rather than continuing to patch `StreamingSession` if a different base is chosen.

## 4. Related Work

### PR #27058: Radix-tree-native session eviction

PR #27058 (`--enable-session-radix-cache`) makes session nodes ordinary evictable radix tree entries tagged with a `session_id`. The tree's own LRU reclaims them at node granularity under pressure; `close_session` scans for the tag to free them on explicit close.

The key difference is the **unit of eviction**. PR #27058 evicts individual nodes by their own `last_access_time`  which is a session's KV can be partially evicted with no agent-level recency concept. Our approach evicts whole sessions ordered by `last_active_time` (when the agent last completed a turn), which is semantically more meaningful for agentic workloads.

# feat: first-class session identity in SGLang
## Labels
- run-ci
- run-ci-extra
Adds a scalar top-level `session_id` as stable request identity and wires it through native, Engine, OpenAI, Responses, and gRPC entry points. This keeps continual-prompt `session_params` unchanged while letting the existing session radix cache use `session_id` without requiring `/open_session` .

### How This Was Implemented
* Keep `session_params` on the existing opened `SessionController` path.
* Use top-level `session_id` as the sole identity for radix-session tagging when `--enable-session-radix-cache` is enabled.
* Keep cache policy gated in the cache, so carrying identity alone does not activate session-radix behavior.
* Separate radix release from the legacy/streaming `release_session` hook.
Walkthrough
* Request adapters pass the scalar `session_id` through tokenization into `Req` .
* The scheduler routes `session_params` and `session_id` independently and rejects native requests that set both.
* Radix sessions begin implicitly on first use and release tagged KV through `/close_session` ; legacy sessions retain `/open_session` semantics.

### Validation
* `247 passed, 25 subtests passed` across request normalization, OpenAI adapters, session caches, and server arguments.
* Rust gRPC request mapping test passes.
* Repository pre-commit checks and protobuf validation pass.
* Live Llama 3.2 1B: radix sessions worked without open, reused 11 cached tokens, and reclaimed tagged KV on close.
* On the same flag-enabled server, `/open_session` plus `session_params` continued through `SessionController` and closed independently.

Latest PR Test (Extra): ✅ [Run #28286432136](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/28286432136)
